cards.text: Jacob, Isaac's son, is married to two sisters, Leah and Rachel, and he loves Rachel more (Genesis 25:26; 29:21-30). I bet the air in that house is thick enough to cut with a cookie cutter, friend. But the LORD sees that Leah is unloved.

cards.question: The LORD sees that Leah is unloved. What does He do for her?

answers.text: He gives her flocks of her own
He sends her back to her father

cards.question: Meanwhile, Rachel is having children too.

cards.text: Leah has a baby boy and names him Reuben. She says, “The LORD has seen my affliction.”

cards.question: Baby Reuben is here. What does Leah hope will happen now?
Leah has a second son and names him Simeon. She says the LORD has heard that she is ___, so He gave her this son as well.

cards.text: Then son number three: Levi. THREE boys in a row, and I can't get three cookies off a tray without dropping one.

cards.question: With her third son, Leah says that now at last Jacob will become attached to her.

cards.text: And once more, son number four: Judah. But listen close, friend, because Leah sounds different this time.

cards.question: When her fourth son, Judah, is born, what does Leah say?

answers.text: This time I will praise the LORD
This time I will ask for a daughter
This time my husband will stay with me

cards.question: After Judah, Leah keeps right on having children, one after another.

cards.text: Now look over at Rachel. Four sons on Leah's side, ZERO on hers, and she envies her sister.

cards.question: Rachel sees she isn't having children for Jacob. What does she say to him?

answers.text: Give me children or I will die
Pray to the LORD for me

cards.question: Jacob gets angry with Rachel. He asks her if he is in the place of ___, who has withheld children from her.

cards.text: So Rachel comes up with Plan B. And I mean B, for Bilhah, her maidservant.

cards.question: Why does Rachel tell Jacob to take her maidservant Bilhah?

answers.text: So Bilhah can bear children for her
So Bilhah can serve Leah instead
So Bilhah can care for the flocks

cards.question: Bilhah becomes Jacob's wife and has a son.

cards.text: Rachel names the boy Dan. She says, “God has vindicated me; He has heard my plea and given me a son.”

cards.question: Bilhah has a second son, and Rachel names him Naphtali. What does Rachel say about it?

answers.text: She has wrestled with her sister and won
She has finally won her father's blessing
She will never envy her sister again

cards.text: Over on Leah's side, she sees she's stopped having children. Four boys, and then nothing.

cards.question: Leah has stopped having children. What does she do next?

answers.text: She gives Jacob her servant Zilpah
She asks Rachel to share Bilhah
She sends Jacob back to Rachel

cards.text: Zilpah has a son, and Leah names him Gad, saying, “How fortunate!” Scoreboard check: Leah's side FIVE, Rachel's side TWO.

cards.question: Zilpah has a second son, and Leah names him Asher. What does Leah say the women call her?

cards.text: Now it's the wheat harvest. Leah's oldest boy, Reuben, goes out into the field and finds something.

cards.question: What does Reuben find in the field during the wheat harvest?
Reuben brings the mandrakes to his aunt Rachel.

cards.text: Rachel begs Leah for some of her son's mandrakes. And Leah is NOT in a sharing mood.

cards.question: Leah asks Rachel if it isn't enough that she has taken away Leah's ___.
Rachel makes Leah a deal. What does Rachel offer her in exchange for the mandrakes?

cards.text: That evening Leah meets Jacob coming in from the field: “You must come with me, for I have hired you with my son’s mandrakes.” The man walks in from a long day at work and finds out he got traded for PLANTS.

cards.question: God listens to Leah, and she has a fifth son.
Leah names her fifth son Issachar. What does she say God has rewarded her for?

answers.text: Giving her maidservant to her husband
Finding the mandrakes in the field

cards.text: Then a sixth son, Zebulun. “God has given me a good gift,” Leah says.

cards.question: Then Leah says this time her husband will ___ her, because she has borne him six sons.

cards.text: After that, Leah has a daughter and names her Dinah. And Rachel? Still no child of her own.

cards.question: God listens to Rachel and opens her womb, just like He did for Leah.
Rachel gives birth to a son and says God has taken away her ___.
Rachel names her son Joseph. What does she say next?

answers.text: May the LORD add to me another son
Now my sister will envy me
Now my husband will honor me

cards.text: We'll set this batch on the cooling rack for now, friend. Trust me, this story's far from done.

findings.problem: The setup line says Leah "sounds different this time." That rules out the wrong answer "This time my husband will stay with me" on card 10, because it sounds just like her earlier hopes for her husband. It leaves the baker only two real options.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: Genesis 30:22 opens with "Then God remembered Rachel." That is a key turn in the passage, and no card tells it or asks about it. Card 17 covers only His listening and opening her womb.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: The story-continues line nearly copies the doc's example ("Trust me, friend, this story's not done" becomes "Trust me, this story's far from done"). It isn't a new line written for this passage.

rule.text: The examples show the idea. Write your own line each time.

findings.problem: This closing card is only the story-continues line and tells no verse, but it cites Genesis 30:24. The citation rule says a story card cites the verses it tells, and this card tells none.
findings.question: When the last story card is only the story-continues line, what should its "verses" field cite: the passage's last verse, the stop's range, or something else?

findings.problem: The "Plan B... B, for Bilhah" joke sits in a passage about trying to conceive and sleeping with a maidservant. Many adults will connect "Plan B" with the emergency contraceptive brand. That brings in an unintended link to sex and contraception, which some see as political, even though the joke means only "backup plan."
findings.question: Should a "Plan B" joke be avoided in childbearing passages because of the contraceptive brand, even when the line only means "backup plan"?
